note: This computes only the first of the three requested differences (SME's annual average minus LAM's): ConQuer's scalar aggregate expressions can combine any number of independent THE ... OF subqueries arithmetically in one query (as in the primer's %-of-female-employees example), but each query yields exactly one number, so the other two differences (LAM-KAM, KAM-SME) need the same pattern re-run with the segment names swapped -- there is no shared enumerable head to LIST all three segments' figures together with a per-group MIN threshold that also varies by group. Also: embedding 'THE MINIMUM ... WHERE date BETWEEN ...' as a live nested subquery (instead of a literal) inside the SUM branch made the query join Yearmonth to Customer twice while re-evaluating the correlated MIN per row-pair, which never returned within 2 minutes even for a single segment; the same MIN embedded in the COUNT branch (only one Yearmonth join) ran fine. So the three per-segment minimum 2013-CZK consumption values were computed separately and first (THE MINIMUM v IN Customer [has CustomerSegment: 'X'] [has CustomerCurrency: 'CZK'] is of Yearmonth [has YearmonthDate d] has YearmonthConsumption v WHERE d >= '201301' AND d <= '201312'), giving SME=-14896.12, LAM=-2458.05, KAM=-582092.86, and plugged in as literals in the SUM branch for performance. Each segment turned out to have exactly one customer at its minimum, so annual average = that customer's total 2013 consumption; verified numbers: SME=153964.61, LAM=242686.29, KAM=170116.39, giving SME-LAM=-88721.68, LAM-KAM=72569.90, KAM-SME=16151.78.
